Oreca 07 - Gibson.historical_insight: The Oreca 07 became the undisputed standard in LMP2, rendering the class nearly a spec series due to its overwhelmingly superior aerodynamic and mechanical performance.

representative_entry.significance: This entry nearly won the 2017 24 Hours of Le Mans overall, finishing second—an unprecedented achievement for an LMP2 car.

Aston Martin Vantage V8.historical_insight: Derived directly from the Vantage road car, the V8 GTE was a thunderous presence in WEC, known for its bonded aluminium chassis and roaring naturally aspirated V8 engine.

representative_entry.significance: A class-winning entry that dominated LMGTE Am, capturing the essence of Aston Martin's GT endurance pedigree.

Porsche 911 RSR.historical_insight: The RSR continuously evolved the iconic 911 platform. In its later iterations (like the 2019 RSR-19), Porsche radically shifted the engine ahead of the rear axle, transforming it into a mid-engined GT powerhouse.

representative_entry.significance: The 'Pink Pig' liveried RSR secured a dominant LMGTE Pro victory at Le Mans, cementing the mid-engined variant's legacy.

Toyota TS050 - Hybrid.historical_insight: The TS050 was a technological tour de force. After heartbreaking near-misses, its 8-megajoule hybrid system ultimately delivered Toyota's long-awaited overall victory at Le Mans.

representative_entry.significance: This lineup secured Toyota's maiden overall victory at the 2018 24 Hours of Le Mans, breaking a decades-long curse.

Porsche 919 Hybrid.historical_insight: The 919 Hybrid defined the LMP1 golden era. Combining a compact V4 engine with advanced dual energy recovery systems, it secured a remarkable three consecutive overall Le Mans wins.

representative_entry.significance: This entry claimed Porsche's 17th overall Le Mans victory, marking their triumphant return to the top step of the podium.
